headline: Positioning flushed, credit still the swing factor: PB data show long liquidation in semis and hyperscalers (memory already de-crowded), Jensen's CoreWeave defence bought a bounce but not a credit repair, and the squeeze moved to crowded software and internet shorts.
market_read: The desks now describe the AI drawdown as long liquidation rather than new shorting: MS PB (Wigg, 15 Oct) saw long sales outpace short adds about 2:1 with memory down to ~4.7% of global nets, UBS PB (Dwyer, 16 Oct) says this unwind is concentrated in semis and hyperscalers and has spread to European semis, and SIG/GS (16 Oct) still put global AI allocation at the 83rd percentile, so the flush is partial. Credit stayed the marginal variable: Jefferies HY (Haber via Titu, 15 Oct) says unsecured at 12-15% leaves equity as the residual funder, GS (Armbrust, 16 Oct) logs HY AI spreads at a 360bp high, and MS credit (Tyler, 16 Oct) is cautious on ORCL, while Jensen Huang's CoreWeave comments (JPM See, Rothschild, 16 Oct) narrowed CRWV CDS by >100bp without bringing it out of distressed territory. The money that left AI went into crowded shorts and laggards: JPM Schilsky (16 Oct) shows APP, RDDT and CRM leading a squeeze, and BofA's Villani (16 Oct) reports the biggest 5-day net selling on its pad in over two years, with Tech ~70% of it. Divergences to watch: META into 21 Oct (UBS: still the top Mag7 long; Bernstein: sentiment worsening on $250-300bn capex), and TSMC (record Taiwan foreign outflow per Jefferies vs capex and estimate raises from MS, BofA and JPM).

up.why: Bloomberg X attention jumped the most in the universe (delta +3.55; 7-day 445 vs a 56 28-day base) with mildly positive tone (+0.08) and the curated X corpus shows the same spike (delta +3.5), around the 3Q print and Friday's CEO webinar. Desk evidence is two-way: JPM sales trading (See, 15 Oct) saw a late buy-the-dip in ASML, and SemiAnalysis (15 Oct) adds a hybrid-bonding optionality story, but UBS PB (Dwyer, 16 Oct) says European semis are now being de-grossed and JPM's Silver (15 Oct) hears high fundamental conviction with deteriorating confidence in the tape. Monitor: HOT 35.8 (20-<40) and BULL 51.0 (40-<60); ASML's own history after this HOT band is -0.8% over 5 sessions (33% up, n=15) and +1.6% over 10 (64% up), after this BULL band +1.3% / +0.6%, descriptive only. 1-5 days: the CEO webinar and EU semis de-grossing dominate; 2-4 weeks: whether LRCX/KLAC prints and any 2027 WFE colour validate the order book.
up.confirm: Buy-the-dip flow repeats on European desks; webinar tone on 2027 holds; EU semis net selling in UBS PB slows.
up.weaken: UBS/JPM report continued European semis long reductions; AMAT-style silence on 2027 WFE from LRCX next week.

up.why: JPM's Schilsky (16 Oct) puts CRM (+5%) in the crowded-short cohort that led the 15 Oct squeeze with APP and RDDT, and Rothschild (16 Oct) lists software names on 3-month relative highs as money rotates out of AI. Monitor: Bloomberg X tone posted the largest rise in the universe (tone +0.29, delta +0.27) on rising attention (delta +1.22) and a +8.3% 7-day return; HOT is only 10.9 (0-<20, no analog history at that level) and BULL 45.7, whose own history is -0.2% over 5 sessions (53% up) and +0.5% over 10 (63% up), descriptive only. 1-5 days: short covering can run while the AI trade is offside; 2-4 weeks: the squeeze needs AI-monetisation evidence (SAP on 21 Oct is the read-across JPM's Silver flagged).
up.confirm: Software keeps outperforming on AI down days; SAP's print shows AI-driven upside; X tone stays positive as attention rises.
up.weaken: AI names rebound and the squeeze reverses; desks describe the move as pure covering with no new longs.

up.why: META is the name with the most inbound into the 21 Oct print (UBS Dwyer, 16 Oct), and the curated X corpus shows attention rising (delta +2.7). The desks disagree on what the attention means: UBS calls it still the top Mag7 long with buy-side capex near $250bn, while Bernstein's Seidman (16 Oct) hears worsening sentiment, $250-300bn capex and low-$30s 2027 EPS vs a mid-$30s Street. No Bloomberg-X analog history for META. 1-5 days: positioning into the print; 2-4 weeks: the 2027 capex/opex framing will drive the hyperscaler and supply-chain read-through.
up.confirm: Desks keep reporting buy-side capex bogeys near or above $250bn without EPS cuts; inbound stays high and constructive.
up.weaken: More desks echo Bernstein's 'worsening sentiment' or a capital-raise read on the early print date.

up.why: Barclays' Rand (16 Oct) says LITE is up 44% off the late-July bottom on in-line revisions because investors now see NPO as the bridge until CPO ramps and LITE as the preferred optical play; MS (Marshall via Wigg, 16 Oct) also favours LITE and COHR in the sell-off on the NPO catalyst, and Jefferies (16 Oct) notes Aixtron orders 30% above consensus on InP demand from optical tightness. Against that, Rothschild (16 Oct) shows optical leading the momentum long-leg selling (LITE -3%, COHR -5%). No Bloomberg-X analog history for LITE. 1-5 days: optical trades as high-beta momentum; 2-4 weeks: NPO evidence from hyperscaler prints.
up.confirm: Optical stops leading the momentum long-leg selling; more desks echo the NPO-bridge framing.
up.weaken: Rothschild/UBS flows show further optical de-grossing; NPO timing talk slips.

down.why: Credit-led weakening, not resolved by the bounce. GS (Armbrust, 16 Oct) logs HY AI spreads at a 360bp high, UBS (Ruple, 16 Oct) still calls CDS ~1,086bp distressed, and Jefferies HY (Haber, 15 Oct) says equity is now the residual funder; Jensen's 'improving every day' claim (JPM See, Rothschild, 16 Oct) narrowed CDS >100bp and the stock closed +6%, but Rothschild reads it as narrative over numbers. Research relays are split: BofA Liani, Jefferies Thill and JPM Chatterjee defend it; Bernstein Rezai stays Underperform. SIG (16 Oct) shows two-way options flow (heavy puts, then a $16m Apr call buy). Monitor: Bloomberg X attention delta +2.47 with tone falling (-0.11, delta -0.15) and a -14.6% 7-day return; HOT 42.6 and BULL 45.6 (both 40-<60); its own history after this BULL band is -4.8% over 5 sessions (33% up, n=15) and +0.4% over 10 (43% up), descriptive only. 1-5 days: credit headlines drive the equity; 2-4 weeks: NBIS (22 Oct) and hyperscaler prints plus any financing.
down.confirm: CDS re-widens above 11-12% or a new debt deal prices wide; X tone keeps falling.
down.weaken: A financing or contract-pricing announcement at short-duration rates; CDS keeps tightening with the stock.

down.why: BofA's Villani (16 Oct) came back from Asia shocked at how bearish investors are on memory after CXMT's 4F2 news (Hynix -21%), and Jefferies (O'Mara, 16 Oct) notes Samsung outperformed Hynix on the HBM equipment-order-cut reports, although Sherman Shang's checks (15 Oct) frame the delay as NVIDIA SLT-software timing rather than an HBM spec issue. JPM (See, 15 Oct) sees KOSPI near peak pain. Monitor: Bloomberg X attention delta +1.19 with tone negative (-0.16, delta -0.15) and a -24.9% 7-day return; HOT 41.2 and BULL 45.1 (40-<60); its own history after these bands is +1.8% / +5.1% over 5 sessions (60% / 70% up) and +4.1% / +4.9% over 10, so this is a sentiment low, not a forecast of further falls. 1-5 days: Korea flows; 2-4 weeks: Jefferies' 22 Oct memory expert call and HBM4 order clarity.
down.confirm: Foreign selling in Korea resumes after Friday's bounce; more reports of HBM4 equipment-order slippage.
down.weaken: The Rubin SLT fix is confirmed quickly; KOSPI holds its July low and foreign flows turn.

down.why: MS PB (Wigg, 15 Oct) shows memory falling from ~13% to ~4.7% of global nets over ~3.5 months, and UBS PB (Dwyer, 16 Oct) says memory was never re-grossed after the summer, so the crowding has already been cleared; BofA's Villani (16 Oct) adds the sentiment overlay (investors 'getting out of the way'). This is easing crowding, distinct from the weakening sentiment in Hynix. Monitor: HOT 45.0 (40-<60), BULL 61.5 (60-<80); MU's own history after this BULL band is -2.3% over 5 sessions (33% up, n=15) and +0.3% over 10 (40% up), descriptive only. 1-5 days: memory moves with Korea; 2-4 weeks: the read from the UBS MU IR call and Jefferies' memory expert call.
down.confirm: PB books keep memory nets near lows while estimates hold; option flows (SIG's DRAM Nov call spreads) stay tentative.
down.weaken: Desks report memory longs being rebuilt or shorts covering aggressively.

down.why: UBS PB (Dwyer, 16 Oct) says this week's de-grossing is concentrated in semis and hyperscalers, MS PB (15 Oct) shows AI data-center beneficiaries down from ~32% to below 20% of US nets, and SIG/GS (16 Oct) call it long liquidation with AI allocation still at the 83rd percentile. Fundamentals are not the complaint: Barclays (Rand, 16 Oct) notes NVIDIA has the largest CY28 revision (+43%) but investors won't buy on valuation alone, and Jensen's BG2 claims (MS, 16 Oct) were bullish. Monitor: HOT 48.7 and BULL 54.3 (40-<60); its own history after these bands is -0.4% / +0.6% over 5 sessions and 0.0% / +3.1% over 10 (52% / 62% up), descriptive only; the curated X corpus shows attention rising (delta +2.8). 1-5 days: momentum unwind vs GTC next week; 2-4 weeks: hyperscaler capex guides.
down.confirm: PB desks report continued semis net selling with gross still elevated; allocation percentiles fall further.
down.weaken: Desks report re-grossing into GTC or hyperscaler prints; semis outperform on a credit-calm day.

down.why: MS credit (Lindsay Tyler via Wigg, 16 Oct) is cautious into the 28 Oct analyst day: 10Y YTW ~150bp wider since the start of 2H, CDS and cash spreads >50bp wider m/m, Moody's Baa3 risk and more ~5-year chip-backed financing; Jefferies' GREED & fear (16 Oct) also cites widening Oracle/CoreWeave spreads. No Bloomberg-X analog for ORCL, so this rests on credit desks alone. 1-5 days: trades with AI credit spreads; 2-4 weeks: the analyst day and any explicit NVIDIA support (the upside risk MS names).
down.confirm: ORCL cash/CDS widen further or a rating-agency action; new chip-backed financing prices wide.
down.weaken: Spreads tighten with CRWV; the analyst day brings financing clarity or partner support.

themes.title: Long liquidation, partially done
themes.text: Three PB books agree the AI drawdown is long selling, not short building: MS (15 Oct) long sales ~2:1 vs short adds with memory nets at ~4.7%; UBS (16 Oct) concentrated in semis and hyperscalers and now in European semis; SIG relaying GS (16 Oct) AI allocation 26.1% but still 83rd percentile. They disagree on how much is left: UBS says gross remains elevated with scope for more de-grossing, JPM sales trading (15 Oct) saw only 4-5/10 urgency, and Jefferies' Japan quant (15 Oct) warns against extrapolating with AI at 17.2x vs 25.6x in July. Weighting in words: PB data first, then desk anecdote.

themes.title: Credit desks diagnose, equity research defends
themes.text: On CoreWeave the split is by function: credit voices (Jefferies HY Haber 15 Oct; GS credit strategy and MS credit 16 Oct) describe a closing unsecured/convert channel and equity as the residual funder, while equity research relayed by desks (BofA Liani, Jefferies Thill, JPM Chatterjee) argues contract economics (~$40M/MW short-duration deals, prepayments, take-or-pay) outweigh funding costs, and Bernstein's Rezai stays Underperform. Jensen Huang's defence is a supplier and shareholder claim (Rothschild notes the ~10% stake). The contract-price $/MW figures quoted are rental contract bases, not the wiki's revenue-per-GW canon.

themes.title: TSMC: capex raises versus record outflows
themes.text: Research relayed through desks raised the capacity path (MS Chan 2027-28 capex $83bn/$92bn; BofA Haas Liu $80-85bn 2027; JPM Hariharan $90bn/$109bn vs buy-side $86bn/$99.5bn) while cutting or holding margins, but Taiwan saw record foreign selling (Jefferies, 16 Oct) and Chris Wood (Jefferies, 16 Oct) says the easy money in semis is made. Capex figures are each broker's own TSMC capex basis and are not reconciled here.

themes.title: SemiAnalysis: ASML into hybrid bonding
themes.text: SemiAnalysis (15 Oct) argues ASML is building a die-to-wafer hybrid-bonding tool on a track architecture, an independent-author view built from patents and a news report, not a company announcement; if right it is a new competitive vector for the hybrid-bonding incumbents. No DAMNANG item arrived in the window.
